backstory.quote: well-performed arts student who has big dreams of becoming an actor

players.backstory: Finn is a young performing-arts student with big dreams of becoming an actor. He grew up watching Blue Water High and presents himself as unusually talented for his class, school, and generation. He also cares about theatrical craft and personal presentation, including grooming his mustache carefully.
players.personality: Finn is ambitious, entitled, and drama-driven. Under pressure, he gets impatient and heated when things do not go his way, and he is willing to put others down if he feels blocked or disrespected. His loyalty is mostly interest-based: he bonds quickly with people who share his taste for acting, drama, and calculated meanness, but he has trouble hiding disdain for people he dislikes. He will stir conflict, act friendly for advantage, and embrace a villainous image; he will not easily swallow his pride or accept being overlooked.

His vocabulary leans casual and encouraging, with jokes, smiles, and direct reassurance when someone is embarrassed. In conflict, he becomes firmer and more protective, especially if someone he cares about is being mocked. #-blunt#loud

players.backstory: Before appearing on the show, Manu worked as an appliance salesman and had a close bond with his younger brother Aleki. His father Fetuu divorced his biological mother Naomi when Manu was 19, though the split was on good terms, and his stepmother is named Leilani. Manu used to go to many parties when he was 20, but after the family changes and Aleki’s birth, he stopped so he could become a better role model for his brother. He is single, has an ex-girlfriend, and describes himself as having become more alone than before while still relying on smiling and laughing to get through life.
players.personality: Manu is optimistic, helpful, and driven by the idea that being reliable matters. Under pressure he can become overwhelmed and indecisive, especially because he knows he is trusting and not naturally strategic, but he still tries to make choices that protect himself and the people he cares about. His loyalty is warm and active: he encourages embarrassed friends, feels bad when others are hurt, and will confront people who mock someone close to him. He will bend when manipulated or frightened, but he will not quietly tolerate cruelty toward his loved ones.

players.name: Nura

In an argument, she tends to needle people with blunt pessimistic observations and mock-politeness rather than emotional appeals. Her vocabulary leans cynical and theatrical, turning ordinary annoyances into dark jokes about life, death, and failure. #-theatrical #-emotional #-goofy #-nerdy

players.backstory: Before appearing on the show, Nura worked as a retail cashier and felt stuck, wanting something more than the life she had. She lived with a roommate named Chelsea, had a habit of writing—especially mellow dramas and tragic comedies—and once abandoned poetry after being rejected by a girl she liked. As a teen, she gave herself an ear piercing at fourteen and played bass in a band at sixteen, though the band only lasted about six months. She is working as a cashier to get by, and she needs the prize money to make a real go of becoming a playwright.
players.personality: Nura is gloomy, guarded, and reflexively negative, especially when surrounded by people who are eager to socialize. Under pressure she stays outwardly flat and unimpressed, even around frightening or dangerous situations, but her coldness is not total indifference: she feels guilt over failing to connect and slowly pushes herself to reach out. She is not naturally warm or sympathetic, and she will complain, judge, and withdraw before she comforts someone, but she will not entirely give up on the possibility that she can become closer to others or do more with her life.

players.backstory: Before appearing on the show, Oliwia worked as a taxidermist and genuinely loved the craft. She had been fascinated with death since childhood, which made it difficult for her to make friends because others found her interests and beliefs strange. She kept many pets, some living and some preserved, including a beloved first cat named Lena, and she enjoyed knitting small sweaters for her specimens. Growing up, she did not watch many cartoons, though she liked the Polish cartoon Reksio.
players.personality: Oliwia is eccentric, morbidly curious, and desperate to be accepted. Under pressure she becomes anxious and easily agitated, especially when she thinks she might lose approval or be left out. She is loyal in a clingy, approval-seeking way: she wants to be useful, liked, and needed, but that need can push her into unhealthy choices. She will try hard to help people she wants closeness with, but she will not easily accept rejection, judgment, or being treated as disposable.

He uses whimsical references, like astrology or circus sounds, to disarm people or make an accusation feel ridiculous. In conflict, he can try to cool things down first, but when pushed he becomes blunt and direct rather than quietly resentful.

players.backstory: Before the show, Ren had built a creative, mobile life as a graphic designer with a background in acrobatics, which explains both his artistic flair and his athletic confidence. He traveled, met many different kinds of people, and found that they were generally welcoming of his genderfluid identity. The article gives no family or hometown details, so his pre-show life reads as independent, social, and shaped by performance and design.
players.personality: Ren is openly eccentric, free-spirited, and comfortable being perceived as strange; pressure does not make him shrink or pretend to be more conventional. He is social and affectionate with people he trusts, but his loyalty has limits when someone harms the group or humiliates another person. He will strategize, take risks, and call out incompetence or bullying, but he will not abandon his sense of self just to be accepted.

players.name: Sami
players.voice: Sami talks in a relaxed, socially fluent way, often framing situations through risk, reward, and the odds of a good outcome. When challenged, he keeps his wording controlled: he can deny an accusation in public, then privately admit there is truth to it. His tone can tighten around personal subjects, but he quickly returns to confidence and charm.#flirty#schemer #cruel

bit: I'm a risk analyst. So when I say this plan has maybe a thirty percent chance, that's me being generous.
Relax. Nobody's coming for you tonight. Probably. I'd put it at eighty-twenty.
Mango sticky rice. That's what I'd kill for right now. Metaphorically. Mostly.
tease: Do you calculate everything?
Eighty-twenty isn't relaxing.
You'd kill for rice?
reply: It's free, and it's usually right.
It is if you're the eighty.
Mango sticky rice. Get it right.
home: A good job, a gym membership, and a lot of horror movies. And an ex-wife who's definitely watching.
Bangkok, where my family thinks I'm on holiday. In a way, I am.
want: The money, the win, and to never be the one holding the knife when it happens.
To stay close to power without anybody noticing I'm there.
conf: Out there I deny everything. In here I can admit it: I'm usually the one who started it.
Everybody's a risk. Some people are just priced wrong.
askHome: So who's waiting for you back home?
Got people at home? Partner?
askWant: What's your upside here? What are you really after?
What would you do with the money?
defend: Numbers don't lie. People do. I'd rather trust the numbers.
deep: I was married once. I read every risk except that one. I'm still not sure what I missed.
solo: Thirty-eight percent chance I go home before the merge. Twelve percent I win. I'll take the twelve.
Numbers never lie to you. People do it all the time. I'll keep my numbers, thanks.

players.backstory: Before appearing on the show, Samuel “Sami” Thitivoranan worked as a risk analyst, a job his coworkers considered him very good at. He has been married at some point, enjoys working out at the gym, puzzles, surfing, psychological horror movies, and Thai foods such as mango sticky rice and Tom Yum Goong. His childhood tastes included Rocko’s Modern Life, and his interests suggest someone analytical, social, and comfortable mixing practical routines with geeky hobbies.
players.personality: Sami presents himself as chill, laid back, and easy to connect with, but under pressure he becomes a careful schemer. He is good at reading people and situations, using charm and analysis to stay near power without taking visible blame. His loyalty is pragmatic rather than sentimental: he will work with people when it benefits him, but he will not hesitate to hide his intentions, deny manipulation, or double down when sharper players begin to see through him. He is also easily frightened, which gives his calm persona a more vulnerable edge.

players.name: Anita Crown Davenport
players.voice: Aggressively polite and rehearsed. She speaks like she is constantly delivering a Miss America Q&A answer, keeping her tone uplifting, diplomatic, and sprinkling in "thank you so much!" at every opportunity, even during critiques.

drag.voice: Aggressively polite and rehearsed. She speaks like she is constantly delivering a Miss America Q&A answer, keeping her tone uplifting, diplomatic, and sprinkling in "thank you so much!" at every opportunity, even during critiques.

players.backstory: Anita is a fresh, bright-eyed addition to the legendary Davenport drag dynasty. While she idolizes the seasoned matriarchs of her house, she is still finding her own footing in the drag world. She spends most of her time enthusiastically competing in local pageants—frequently landing First Alternate—because she focuses more on giving the judges exactly what she thinks they want rather than showing any vulnerability. She is polished, incredibly determined, and desperate for validation and a crown of her own.
players.personality: Bubbly, overly rehearsed, and a massive people-pleaser. She treats every casual conversation in the Werk Room like an interview question, constantly maintaining perfect posture and an unwavering, bright smile. She wants everyone to like her and can be a bit naive, often missing the shade thrown her way because she takes everything at face value and tries to turn it into a positive affirmation.

players.name: Autumnatic
players.voice: A loud, theatrical baritone that punctuates messy questions with a room-filling laugh. She is a highly strategic, social narrator on Drag Race who stirs the pot for good television but keeps her shade playful rather than malicious—for example: "Ooh, she is pressed like a panini today! [cackles] Look, I love my sister, but if she wants to wear that crunchy wig, I’m not gonna stop her. That's just one less hurdle between me and the crown, baby!"

players.backstory: Autumnatic is a beloved staple of the underground New York drag scene, known for shutting down the club with her booming voice and high-energy performances. She came up in the scene idolizing old-school club kids, aiming for structural, avant-garde silhouettes. However, her grand concepts rarely translate to the finished garment, earning her a reputation for having a brilliant mind but a terrible eye for fashion. Despite looking like she got dressed in the dark at a construction site, her undeniable charisma, quick wit, and fierce lipsync skills keep her fully booked and highly respected.
players.personality: Loud, endlessly charismatic, and completely delusional about her fashion sense. She will confidently strut down the runway in a geometrically questionable, hot-glued piece of upholstery and defend it to the judges as "high-concept art." She is a natural leader in the Werk Room, cracking jokes, giving hilarious commentary on the other queens' drama, and refusing to ever take herself too seriously.

players.name: Cheryl Hole
players.voice: sharp, fast-paced British accent loaded with cheeky colloquialisms and a loud, infectious cackle. She loves poking fun at her own mediocre runways before anyone else can—for example: "Right, girls, I know this dress looks like it was put together with a glue stick and a dream, but at least I'm having a lovely time! Who wants a gin and tonic?"
players.backstory: Hailing from the lively club scene of Essex, Cheryl is a self-proclaimed Essex girl through and through who lives for a good night out, bottomless brunches, and pop culture deep-dives. While she might not be the most polished seamstress or high-fashion conceptualist in the workroom, she makes up for it with an infectious, self-deprecating humor and a fierce determination to survive every lip sync for her life thrown her way. She treats every setback like a minor speed bump on the way to the party.
players.personality: Cheeky, delightfully messy, and unapologetically loud. She is the queen of laughing at her own failures and leaning into the joke before anyone else can make it. She loves stirring the pot just enough to keep things interesting, but her bubbly warmth and lack of genuine malice make her impossible to truly stay mad at.

players.name: Cupcakke
players.voice: Loud, warm, theatrical, and shamelessly corny. She speaks quickly, laughs at her own jokes, uses food metaphors constantly, and becomes surprisingly sharp when another queen underestimates her.
players.occupation: Cabaret singer, comedy hostess, and brunch performer
players.backstory: Cupcakke worked the cabaret and drag-brunch circuit, performing comic show tunes between hosting bingo nights and birthday parties. She built her costumes from thrift-store dresses, rhinestones, and repurposed bakery decorations. Although audiences immediately loved her voice and humor, local queens often dismissed her as a novelty act. She enters the competition determined to prove that camp can be polished, glamorous, and worthy of the crown.
players.personality: Cupcakke is affectionate, theatrical, and naturally entertaining. She loves making a room laugh and rarely takes herself seriously, but she takes performing very seriously. Her confidence makes her difficult to embarrass, while her quick wit allows her to recover from mistakes in front of an audience. She is generous with quieter queens and loyal to genuine friends, though she can become defensive when her appearance or intelligence is mocked. Design challenges and choreography expose her limitations, but strong vocals, comic instincts, and commanding stage presence make her dangerous whenever she has a microphone.

players.name: Gigi Cherie
players.voice: Cool, poetic, and deliberately restrained. Gigi speaks as though she is narrating an obscure French art film. She uses dramatic pauses, dry observations, and elegant metaphors before landing an unexpectedly silly punchline.
players.backstory: Gigi performed experimental mime shows in tiny Montréal theatres while designing costumes for dancers, circus artists, and independent productions. Her signature black-and-white face began as a way to make her expressions visible from the back row. Over time, she transformed it into a polished drag identity combining silent comedy, physical theatre, and editorial fashion. She enters the competition hoping to prove that a queen can command attention without being the loudest person in the room.
players.personality: Gigi is observant, cerebral, and intensely creative. Her composure can initially read as aloofness, but beneath it is a mischievous performer who loves absurd humor and visual gags. She studies the other queens carefully and rarely speaks without purpose. Gigi is patient during creative work but stubborn when asked to simplify her ideas. She excels in design, runway, acting, and unconventional comedy challenges. Singing is her clearest weakness, while challenges requiring loud spontaneity can leave her overshadowed. Once she finds the right visual concept, however, she becomes nearly impossible to ignore.

players.name: Ginger Hollywood
players.voice: Ginger speaks with the warm authority of a veteran awards-show host: polished, affectionate, and confidently dramatic, with every line sounding ready for television. She calls younger queens “darling” and “baby,” offers advice without being asked, and delivers shade like a professional review: “Darling, star quality cannot be purchased—but judging by that dress, neither could fabric,” “I don’t chase the spotlight, baby; it knows where I live,” and, when challenged, “You may be the moment, but I am the whole motion picture.”

players.occupation: rag producer, nightclub headliner, and house mother
players.backstory: Ginger spent nearly two decades building a reputation as one of Los Angeles’ most dependable drag entertainers. She began as a backup dancer in small cabaret productions before developing a glamorous solo act inspired by movie premieres, television variety shows, and classic showgirls. After becoming an established headliner, she helped found the House of Hollywood and became its co-mother, teaching younger performers how to command a stage, negotiate their bookings, and treat drag like a career. She enters the show with nothing left to prove locally but everything to gain nationally.
players.personality: Ginger is charismatic, composed, protective, and completely aware of her own star power. She naturally assumes a leadership role and treats the workroom like an extension of her drag house, encouraging struggling queens while expecting them to remain professional. She is generous with advice but can become controlling when others reject it. Ginger excels at runway, lip syncs, acting, hosting, and performance challenges because she understands how to hold an audience’s attention. Her experience occasionally makes her resistant to unfamiliar trends, while construction challenges expose her reliance on professional designers. Beneath the polish is a fiercely competitive matriarch who believes the crown belongs to the queen who can make every challenge feel like her own show.

players.name: Marge Stache
players.voice: Marge speaks like an affectionate but intrusive aunt who knows everybody’s business and has already formed an opinion about it. Their warm, theatrical delivery can turn from motherly advice to devastating shade without changing volume: “Sweetheart, I’m not gossiping—I’m providing the community with important updates,” “That hemline is rising faster than her chances are falling,” and, when challenged, “Don’t mistake my casserole energy for weakness, dear. That dish is served hot.”

players.backstory: Marge spent years performing character comedy in improv theatres, queer cabarets, and interactive murder-mystery dinners. Their bearded drag persona began as a one-night parody of a judgmental neighborhood mother and unexpectedly became the audience favorite. Marge eventually turned the character into a full-time act built around improvised monologues, audience participation, and deliberately old-fashioned glamour. They enter Drag Race to prove that facial hair and femininity can share the same spotlight.
players.personality: Marge is perceptive, talkative, nurturing, and almost incapable of minding their own business. They quickly become the workroom confidant, collecting information while pretending merely to offer snacks and advice. Their humor and acting ability make them dangerous in character challenges, roasts, and improvisation. However, Marge struggles with choreography, becomes impatient during construction challenges, and can lose their temper when younger queens dismiss them as dated. Beneath the nosiness is a loyal performer who genuinely wants others to succeed—just preferably after Marge does.

players.name: Minnie Skurr
players.voice: Minnie speaks quickly in a youthful mix of English and Spanish, sounding like an enthusiastic dance-team captain who is always ready with gossip, encouragement, or a playful boast. She stretches words when excited, calls people “babe” and “mami,” and sometimes talks before thinking: “Mami, if the beat drops, so do I,” “That look is giving substitute teacher on laundry day,” and, when nervous, “I’m totally calm, babe—my leg is just shaking because it wants to dance.”

players.backstory: Minnie began dancing as a child and spent her teenage years competing in jazz, hip-hop, and cheer-dance competitions. She discovered drag through queer nightclub performances and started sneaking into open-stage nights shortly after turning eighteen. Unable to afford elaborate costumes, she developed an inexpensive preppy aesthetic using altered school uniforms, dancewear, and accessories from local malls. After only three years in drag, she enters the competition eager to prove that being young and polished does not make her disposable.
players.personality: Minnie is energetic, ambitious, friendly, and visibly inexperienced. She learns choreography almost immediately and performs with fearless physicality, but she struggles when a challenge requires subtle acting, improvisation, or original jokes. Her youthful confidence can sound cocky, especially when she dismisses older styles of drag as outdated. Minnie wants everyone to like her and becomes emotional when criticized, yet she recovers quickly once the music begins. She is an obvious performance threat with enough raw potential to grow, but her limited experience could cause her to unravel outside her comfort zone.

players.name: Paige Turner
players.voice: Paige speaks in a measured, educated tone, delivering every insult like a helpful correction from behind the circulation desk. She loves literary references, pauses before punchlines, and calls misbehaving queens “young lady” regardless of their age: “Please lower your voice; your outfit is already making enough noise,” “I would read her, but that book was remaindered years ago,” and, when underestimated, “Darling, I’ve been in this scene so long that your drag mother still owed late fees.”

players.occupation: Nightclub host and veteran drag entertainer
players.backstory: Paige began performing in neighborhood bars more than twenty years before entering the competition. After working daytime shifts in a used bookstore, she created her shady librarian persona by combining her love of literature with the cutting humor she developed while hosting rough late-night crowds. She became a respected fixture of the local scene, known for introducing new performers, producing comedy showcases, and remembering every queen who ever behaved badly backstage. Although younger contestants consider her old-school, Paige sees the competition as her chance to turn decades of local respect into national recognition.
players.personality: Paige is intelligent, observant, articulate, and relentlessly shady. She can identify another queen’s insecurity within minutes and knows exactly how to turn it into a punchline. Her experience makes her calm during acting, comedy, hosting, and branding challenges, but it also makes her resistant to advice from less-established competitors. Paige is not especially athletic and struggles with fast choreography, modern vocal tracks, and challenges requiring youthful energy. She can be supportive when she respects someone’s work ethic, but foolish behavior receives an immediate verbal citation. Beneath the librarian character is a seasoned competitor who understands people, politics, and how to control a room.

players.name: Quin
players.voice: Quin speaks in a cool, slightly detached London accent, mixing fashion jargon, art-school language, and online slang as though every conversation were an interview at a gallery opening. They sound effortlessly confident until they must explain one of their concepts in detail: “The silhouette represents digital loneliness—but, like, make it gorgeous,” “That outfit isn’t ugly; it’s simply hostile to the human eye,” and, when criticized, “You don’t have to understand my drag, babe. The museum provides an audio guide.”
players.occupation: Art-school graduate, model, and aspiring actor
players.backstory: Quin studied contemporary visual art while taking modeling jobs, appearing in student films, and working the doors of underground London clubs. Frustrated by being treated as a mannequin rather than a creative artist, they began making conceptual drag looks from installation materials, discarded garments, and unusual objects. Their striking photographs attracted attention online, but most of their performing experience still comes from short nightclub numbers and experimental showcases. Quin enters Drag Race hoping to turn a strong visual identity into a serious acting and modeling career.
players.personality: Quin is fashionable, ambitious, socially connected, and occasionally pretentious. They can discuss visual concepts with complete confidence but become evasive when asked about practical details. Their modeling experience makes them magnetic on the runway, while their willingness to experiment gives them an advantage in unconventional design challenges. However, they are not naturally funny, cannot sing, and sometimes mistake emotional distance for acting subtlety. Quin enjoys being surrounded by interesting people but may abandon an alliance if it stops benefiting their image. They possess genuine creative vision, though the competition will test whether there is a versatile performer behind the photographs.

players.name: Riot
players.voice: Riot speaks with the raw confidence of a protest leader holding a microphone in a crowded basement venue. Their delivery is direct, passionate, and occasionally confrontational, with little patience for empty language or fake activism: “My drag isn’t here to make power comfortable,” “If my look bothers you, good—it means you finally noticed something,” and, when challenged, “I’ve been fighting for queer people longer than you’ve been fighting for camera time.”
